Quirk Drawbacks and the Body.text: Every Quirk has a cost, because every Quirk runs through a body. Emitters strain whatever produces their effect: a fire user overheats, a sound user strains their throat, a user who burns body fat, sugar or water runs dry and has to eat or drink, an electric user who overloads is left dazed and slow. Transformations end in fatigue, soreness or a vulnerable recovery period. Mutant bodies can need more food, special care or gear built for them. Some Quirks have recoil: a power stronger than its user's frame can tear muscle or break bone with each use. Others come with conditions: a maximum duration, a cooldown, a trigger that needs line of sight, a sense lost while the Quirk is active. Pushing past a limit is possible and dangerous, and a hero who ignores the cost is called reckless, not brave. Bodies adapt. Repeated, careful use builds tolerance, and training the muscles, lungs and nerves around a Quirk raises its safe ceiling. Hero academies track each student's limits, and at U.A. Academy Recovery Girl heals injuries by drawing on the patient's own stamina, so even treatment costs something. Support gear manages many drawbacks with cooling layers, recoil-absorbing gauntlets and supply packs. No training or gear removes a drawback entirely, and the most respected pros are the ones who know exactly where their own limits lie.
